cases.title: Fleet capacity and downstream capacity constrain failover
cases.prompt: Review sizing.md and assess the peak-load and zone-loss claims. Show the relevant calculations, binding constraints, and evidence needed for a defensible sizing decision. Keep this read-only.

rubric.criterion: Calculates 2160 nominal normal replica throughput and 1440 after one zone loss, and rejects the 1500 peak zone-loss claim even under the linear estimate.
Identifies the measured 1400 database workload capacity as an additional binding constraint rather than solving the proposal solely by adding replicas.
Accounts for startup/cold-cache/retry assumptions and proposes representative fleet and failure-state validation, with estimates clearly labeled.
Leaves the supplied fixture unchanged and distinguishes proposed checks from executed runtime evidence.

cases.title: Continuing arrivals and startup delay determine drain time
cases.prompt: Assess queue.md against the ten-minute recovery objective. Derive a drain-time estimate with its assumptions and explain whether the proposed scale-up is sufficient. Do not edit files.

rubric.criterion: Computes 12000 jobs after startup, a net drain rate of 20 jobs/s, and total recovery time of 720 seconds under the stated assumptions.
Recognizes that finishing by 600 seconds needs at least 65 jobs/s after startup under this model, exceeding the measured dependency limit.
Preserves all accepted jobs and includes effect correctness, byte/age constraints, variation and measured recovery validation.
Leaves the supplied fixture unchanged and distinguishes proposed checks from executed runtime evidence.

cases.title: An inventory request does not require sizing
cases.prompt: Read inventory.md and list the supplied deployment names and replica counts only. Keep the file unchanged; there is no sizing or capacity recommendation requested.

rubric.criterion: Does not load capacity-planning or invent a headroom analysis for a request to list inventory.
Returns api 3, importer 2 and notifier 1 without unsupported sizing advice.
Leaves the supplied fixture unchanged and distinguishes proposed checks from executed runtime evidence.
